ML-01.title: — Machine Learning — End-to-End Modelling Masterclass
ML-01.one_screen: **Problem → Data → Baseline → Diagnose → Model → Validate → Tune → Explain → Stress → Deploy → Monitor** --- `Business problem` → `Target + prediction unit` → `Metric` → `Data audit` → `Train / Validation / Test` → `EDA` → `Pre-processing` → `Simple baseline` → `Linear / Logistic` → `Regularisation` → `Decision Tree` → `Bagging / Random Forest` → `Boosting / Gradient Boosting` → `ANN` → `Cross-validation` → `Hyperparameter tuning` → `Calibration / Threshold` → `Explainability` → `Error analysis` → `Stress / robustness` → `Final untouched test` → `Deployment` → `Monitoring / retraining` **Never jump to the most complex model first. ** Start simple → understand errors → add complexity only when it solves a demonstrated problem.  --- **Observation unit** → customer / loan / transaction / month?

ML-02.title: Business Objective ≠ ML Metric
ML-02.one_screen: Example: “Identify borrowers likely to default. ” Still incomplete.  Need: `Business decision` → `Prediction` → `Cost of errors` → `Metric` → `Threshold` --- `Train` → learn parameters `Validation` → choose models / hyperparameters `Test` → final unbiased estimate Typical conceptual split: **Train / Validation / Test** or **Train + Cross-validation / Test** --- Never randomly mix future and past.

ML-03.title: Initial Data Audit
ML-03.one_screen: Before EDA: --- Regression: - distribution - skew - zeros - tails Classification: - class proportions - rare-event severity Numeric: `distribution` → `relationship` → `non-linearity` → `outliers` Categorical: `category frequency` → `target rate by category` Check: - correlation - redundant variables - multicollinearity - duplicate information - interaction opportunities --- Missingness itself can contain information.  Blindly drop rows without checking whether removal changes population.  --- Three possibilities: `Data error` → correct / remove `Valid extreme` → retain `Valid but destabilising` → transform / winsorise / robust model - Linear Regression - Logistic Regression - KNN - SVM - ANN Much less sensitive to scaling and monotonic transformations.

ML-06.title: Multicollinearity
ML-06.one_screen: Predictors explain each other.  Consequences: - unstable coefficients - large standard errors - coefficient signs can flip - interpretation becomes difficult Higher VIF: → stronger multicollinearity.  - remove redundant variable - combine variables - PCA - Ridge - accept if prediction is good and inference is not priority --- Easy interpretation.

ML-07.title: Logistic Statistical Tests
ML-07.one_screen: Tests individual coefficient.  Compare: `Restricted model` vs `Larger model` Tests whether added parameters meaningfully improve likelihood.  --- Of predicted positives, how many were correct?

ML-08.title: Regularisation
ML-08.one_screen: Controls model complexity.  General objective: --- Effect: → shrinks coefficients → usually retains all predictors Best when: - many correlated variables - stability needed --- Effect: → some coefficients become exactly zero Useful for: - sparse model - embedded feature selection --- Useful when: - many predictors - correlated groups - some sparsity desired --- **High bias** - train poor - validation poor Need: → more flexible model → better features → less regularisation --- **High variance** - train excellent - validation poor Need: → simpler model → more data → stronger regularisation → pruning → bagging → early stopping --- Compare performance as training data increases.  Train poor + Validation poor → **underfitting** Train strong + Validation weak, gap remains → **overfitting** Both improve and converge → healthy Validation still improving strongly with more data → more data may help --- Tree recursively asks: `Feature` → `Split` → `Branch` → `Leaf prediction` Example: `Income < threshold?

ML-09.title: Controlling Tree Complexity
ML-09.one_screen: Important parameters: Smaller tree: → more bias → less variance Larger tree: → less bias → more variance --- Core idea: **Combine weak / unstable models into a stronger predictor. ** Two major families: Models built **independently / parallel** Goal: → reduce variance Models built **sequentially** Goal: → correct previous errors --- **Bootstrap Aggregating** Process: `Original Train` → sample with replacement → fit Model 1 → another bootstrap → Model 2 → ...  Predictions: Regression: Classification: → average probabilities / vote.

ML-10.title: Random Forest Tuning
ML-10.one_screen: General pattern: More trees: → lower ensemble variance → more computation → usually not more overfitting in the same way as deeper individual trees.  --- Each bootstrap tree excludes some training observations.  Those excluded cases: → **OOB observations** Use them to estimate performance without a separate validation prediction for that tree.

It is **not**: - probability that null is true - probability result happened by chance - measure of business importance - model-performance metric Large datasets can make tiny, practically meaningless effects statistically significant.  --- Prediction only requires association.

ML-20.title: Final Interview Cheat Sheet
ML-20.one_screen: **Continuous target → linear conditional mean → OLS → coefficients → residual assumptions → MAE/RMSE/R²** **Binary target → log-odds → probability → odds ratios → discrimination + calibration → threshold** **L1 = sparse** **L2 = shrink** **Elastic Net = both** **Recursive splits → nonlinear + interactions → interpretable → high variance** **Independent bootstrap models → average → variance ↓** **Bagging + random features → decorrelated trees → robust ensemble** **Sequential weak learners → correct previous errors** **Fit residuals/gradients → learning rate × trees → powerful tabular model** **Weighted layers → activations → loss → backprop → gradient optimisation → deep nonlinear representation** **Train learns** **CV/Validation chooses** **Test proves** **Best model ≠ most complex model.  Best model = strongest repeatable out-of-sample solution to the actual business problem.
